samples.summary: The api-keys create ordering fix (validate --format *before* minting the key) has no test
samples.evidence: api-keys.ts:21-22 adds `const fmt = parseOutputFormat(opts.format);` above `createApiKey(name)` with a comment stating the whole rationale: "a bad `--format` must not discard a raw key that the server will never show again." No test asserts this ordering. I globbed packages/cli/test/**/*.ts and grepped the package for `createApiKey` — the only non-src hits are packages/cli/src/*, and there is no api-keys test file at all. The new test/status.test.ts wires only status, ctx and schema (lines 128-134). Swapping the two lines back (validating after the POST) would leave every test green, so the safety-critical behavior this hunk exists for is uncovered. The same 'validate before the side effect' ordering is untested for the other write commands too (docs create/rename/delete, notes, slides, cells set/delete/batch, sheets import).
searchedFor: read test/status.test.ts run() helper (only status/ctx/schema registered)

samples.summary: New `cell()` nested-value handling is only tested on the record path; the array path still uses String() and no test covers it
samples.evidence: table.ts introduces `cell()` (lines 7-10) to JSON-serialize nested values, but only `formatRecord` (line 24) uses it; the array branch still calls `String(row[k] ?? '')` at line 53. The new tests exercise nested values only via a single object (`schema ctx.list --format table`, status.test.ts:236-241) and simple scalars (output.test.ts formatTable single-object cases). No test feeds an array of objects containing a nested object/array to formatTable, so the remaining `[object Object]` path is entirely uncovered and the asymmetry is invisible to the suite.

samples.summary: 'renders every field under --format table' checks 3 of 8 fields and its `[object Object]` assertion cannot fail
samples.evidence: status.test.ts:81-87 titles itself 'renders every field' but only asserts three substrings (user, server, 'valid'). The `expect(table).not.toContain('[object Object]')` guard is vacuous here: buildStatus(makeSession()) returns only primitive values (status.ts buildStatus), so `String()` alone would never produce `[object Object]` — the assertion holds identically with or without the new `cell()` helper. Fields email, workspaceId, workspaceName, expiresAt, loggedIn are unasserted, so dropping any of them from the table renderer keeps the test green.

samples.summary: 'is JSON-parseable' tests are near-tautological JSON round-trips rather than the emitted contract
samples.evidence: status.test.ts:74-79 does `JSON.parse(format(buildStatus(x),'json')).loggedIn` and re-asserts the same boolean that the adjacent buildStatus tests already assert; ctx.test.ts's 'is JSON-parseable as emitted by the default format' (`JSON.parse(format(rows,'json'))).toEqual(rows)`) likewise only proves JSON.stringify/JSON.parse round-trips, which is true of any serializable value. Neither can fail for a reason specific to this change; the real command-level JSON contract is covered instead by the wiring tests at status.test.ts:154-210.

samples.summary: The --quiet branch of the new error paths (INVALID_FORMAT / NOT_LOGGED_IN) is untested
samples.evidence: outputError (formatter.ts:78-88) suppresses the JSON body but still sets exitCode 1 under --quiet. The only new --quiet test (status.test.ts:220-225) covers the success path (`status --quiet` → no stdout, exit 0). No test runs e.g. `status --format bogus --quiet` or `ctx list --quiet` to assert stderr stays silent while exitCode becomes 1, which is the agent-facing contract for the two new error codes this change introduces.
searchedFor: grep quiet in packages/cli/test/status.test.ts and output.test.ts

samples.summary: `status --format csv` test asserts only the header row, not the emitted values
samples.evidence: status.test.ts:163-166 asserts `lastStdout().split('\n')[0] === 'loggedIn,message'`. It never checks the data row, so a CSV renderer that emitted correct headers with empty/garbled values (or mis-serialized the boolean `false`) would pass. It also only covers the logged-out payload; the logged-in 8-field CSV — the case where csv escaping of the workspace name with an apostrophe/comma actually matters — is untested.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: api-keys.ts:20-27 does place parseOutputFormat before createApiKey with a rationale comment about not discarding a once-shown raw key, but no test anywhere exercises the api-keys create action. Repo-wide grep for createApiKey/api-keys shows the only test hits are structural: namespaces.test.ts (command/alias existence) and schema.test.ts (registry names/safety). status.test.ts's run() helper registers only status/ctx/schema (lines 128-134), so its --format bogus tests never touch a write command. output.test.ts covers parseOutputFormat in isolation, which passes regardless of call ordering inside the action. Backend e2e api-key spec is pure HTTP with no CLI invocation and no --format usage; CLI-roundtrip e2e specs only exercise docs/notes content. The sole other occurrence of ["api-keys","create","x"] is scripts/agent/hunt-probe.test.mjs:162, which asserts the harness REFUSES to run it. Reordering the two lines back would leave the entire suite green, so the behavior this hunk exists for is untested — a clear behavior change with no meaningful coverage (major under the test-adequacy rubric).

finding.summary: The safety-critical ordering in `api-keys create` (validate --format BEFORE minting the key) has no test
finding.evidence: api-keys.ts:21-27 moves `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` above `createApiKey(name)` with a comment stating the whole point: "a bad `--format` must not discard a raw key that the server will never show again." No test exercises this. status.test.ts's wiring suite only registers status/ctx/schema (status.test.ts:130-132); namespaces.test.ts only asserts command names/aliases; grep for `createApiKey`/`registerApiKeysCommand` across packages/cli/test finds no invocation of the action handler. A regression that moved the parse back below the API call (re-introducing the key-loss bug) would keep the suite green, since parseOutputFormat itself is tested only in isolation (output.test.ts:56-72).

verdict.reason: Verified the claimed code and searched repo-wide for a counterexample; none exists. api-keys.ts:20-27 puts parseOutputFormat (line 23) before createApiKey (line 24) with an explicit key-loss rationale comment (lines 21-22). The only tests referencing the command are namespaces.test.ts, which imports registerApiKeysCommand (line 8, 16) but asserts solely on name()/aliases()/options and never calls program.parse, so no action handler executes; and schema.test.ts (lines 32-34, 54, 82-86), which only checks registry names/safety/alias resolution. The single suite that actually drives commander (status.test.ts:128-134) registers only status/ctx/schema, so its --format bogus cases (168-173, 181-185, 230-234) do not touch api-keys. parseOutputFormat is tested only in isolation (output.test.ts:63-68, 130-133), which passes regardless of ordering inside the action. Repo-wide greps for createApiKey, registerApiKeysCommand, and api-keys/api-key outside node_modules surfaced no other harness: scripts/agent/hunt-*.test.mjs only assert that argv like ["api-keys","create","x"] is REFUSED by the agent safety guard (hunt-probe.test.mjs:160-171) and never executes the CLI; packages/backend/test/api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts exercises backend HTTP routes with no CLI --format involvement; docs-content.test.ts:325 is an unrelated authMode string. A regression restoring parse-after-mint would keep the suite green, so this is a behavior change with no meaningful test — major under the test-adequacy rubric.
